In this section, we introduce our proposed approach KQ-SVD for KV cache compression. We consider taking the interaction between queries and keys into account. The method views the key and query matrices as a single entity and applies singular value decomposition (SVD) to  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$ . We begin by outlining the motivation behind this idea, followed by a detailed explanation of the technique.

# 4.1 Motivation

Existing compression methods based on SVD typically compress keys or jointly embed  $\mathbf{Q} / \mathbf{K} / \mathbf{V}$ . Theorem 1 (proof in Appendix A) inspired by [Wang et al., 2025] shows why that can fail: perturbations in  $\mathbf{K}$  are amplified by the inner products  $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}$  and further propagated by the value multiplication.

Theorem 1. Let  $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  be a sequence of token embeddings,  $\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  and

$$
\mathrm {M H A} (\mathbf {X}) = \left[ \mathrm {S o f t m a x} (\mathbf {Q} _ {i} \mathbf {K} _ {i} ^ {\top} / \sqrt {d}) \mathbf {V} _ {i}) \right] _ {i} \mathbf {W} ^ {O},
$$

$$
\widetilde {\mathrm {M H A}} (\mathbf {X}) = \left[ \operatorname {S o f t m a x} (\mathbf {Q} _ {i} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} _ {i} ^ {\top} / \sqrt {d}) \widetilde {\mathbf {V}} _ {i}) \right] _ {i} \mathbf {W} ^ {O},
$$

where  $\widetilde{\mathrm{MHA}} (\mathbf{X}),\widetilde{\mathbf{K}}_i$  and  $\widetilde{\mathbf{V}}_i$  represent the approximation of MHA(X),  $\mathbf{K}_i$  and  $\mathbf{V}_i$  , respectively. The difference between the actual attention output and the one produced with approximate keys and values is upper bounded as

$$
\begin{array}{l} \| \widetilde {\operatorname {M H A}} (\mathbf {X}) - \operatorname {M H A} (\mathbf {X}) \| _ {2} \\ \leq \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {h} \frac {\| \mathbf {V} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} \| _ {2}}{\sqrt {d}} \| \mathbf {Q} _ {i} \mathbf {K} _ {i} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {Q} _ {i} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} _ {i} ^ {\top} \| _ {2} \\ + \left\| \mathbf {V} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} - \widetilde {\mathbf {V}} _ {i} \mathbf {W} _ {i} ^ {O} \right\| _ {2}. \tag {1} \\ \end{array}
$$

The method proposed by this paper stems from the will to minimize this upper bound on the output approximation error. In each attention head, for a key cache  $\mathbf{K}$  and a calibration set of query vectors  $\{\mathbf{q}^{(j)}\}_{j\in \mathrm{calibration}}$  (row vectors of size  $d$ ), we want to minimize

$$
\sum_ {j \in \text {c a l i b r a t i o n}} \| \mathbf {q} ^ {(j)} \mathbf {K} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {q} ^ {(j)} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} ^ {\top} \| _ {2} ^ {2},
$$

over low-rank  $\widetilde{\mathbf{K}}$ . This objective is equivalent to a low-rank approximation of the query-key interaction matrix and admits an optimal closed-form solution via the singular value decomposition. Similarly, to compress values we directly optimize the second term of Eq. (3) over low-rank  $\widetilde{\mathbf{V}}$  for each attention head (see Appendix B).

# 4.2 Proposed Method

In the following, we drop the head index  $i$  for ease of clarity. Our method addresses cache compression by producing an optimal solution to

$$
\min  _ {\widetilde {\mathbf {K}}} \| \mathbf {Q} \mathbf {K} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {Q} \widetilde {\mathbf {K}} ^ {\top} \| _ {F} ^ {2} \text {s . t .} \operatorname {r a n k} (\widetilde {\mathbf {K}}) \leq R,
$$

with  $\mathbf{Q} = \left(\mathbf{q}^{(j)}\right)_{j\in \mathrm{calibration}}$  the collection of query vectors from the calibration set. This formulation jointly considers the properties of both  $\mathbf{K}$  and  $\mathbf{Q}$ , while taking into account their interaction through the inner product. The optimization problem can be restated using a projection matrix as

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {S}} \left\| \mathbf {K S Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \right\| _ {F} ^ {2} \quad \text {s . t .} \operatorname {r a n k} (\mathbf {S}) \leq R,
$$

where  $\mathbf{S} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ . To be able to compress the key cache during the attention computation, we write the projection matrix  $\mathbf{S}$  as a product of two matrices, i.e.,  $\mathbf{S} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{B}$  with  $\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times R}$ . The minimization problem tackled by KQ-SVD is thus

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F} ^ {2}. \tag {2}
$$

Given  $\mathbf{A}^*$  and  $\mathbf{B}^*$  the solutions of this optimization problem, we store the low-rank matrix  $\mathbf{K}\mathbf{A}^{*}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$ , which

allows for compression while maintaining an accurate reconstruction of the attention matrix. The same strategy also applies to the value-output matrices (see Appendix B). In the next section, we state the main theorem which demonstrates that the optimization problem described above admits an optimal solution which can be computed efficiently.

# 4.3 KQ-SVD: Optimal attention factorization

The following theorem establishes the provably optimal low-rank factorization of the key-query matrix, which admits a simple closed-form solution.

Theorem 2. Let  $\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{Q} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  be key and query cache matrices. The optimal solution to the low rank attention approximation problem

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F},
$$

is given by

$$
\mathbf {A} = \mathbf {K} ^ {+} \hat {\mathbf {U}}, \mathbf {B} = \mathbf {K} ^ {T} \hat {\mathbf {U}},
$$

where  $\hat{\mathbf{U}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$  is the matrix having the top  $R$  left singular vectors of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  as columns.

Proof. Observe that  $\mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top}$  has rank at most  $R$ . Hence,

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {d \times R}} \| \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F},
$$

is lower bounded by

$$
\min  _ {\mathbf {M} \in \mathbb {R} ^ {T \times T}} \| \mathbf {M} - \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \| _ {F} \text {s . t . r a n k} (\mathbf {M}) \leq R.
$$

By the Eckart-Young theorem, we know the best rank  $R$  approximation of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  is given by its truncated SVD:

$$
\mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \simeq \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\boldsymbol {\Sigma}} \hat {\mathbf {V}} ^ {\top},
$$

where  $\hat{\mathbf{U}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R},\hat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}\in \mathbb{R}^{R\times R}$  and  $\hat{\mathbf{V}}\in \mathbb{R}^{T\times R}$ . We will show that  $\mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top} = \hat{\mathbf{U}}\hat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}\hat{\mathbf{V}}^{\top}$  from which the optimality of  $\mathbf{A}$  and  $\mathbf{B}$  follows.

Let  $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{U}\pmb{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}$  be the full SVD of  $\mathbf{K}$ . Observe that we have the inclusion of (column) spans:  $\mathcal{R}(\hat{\mathbf{U}})\subseteq \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{U}) = \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K})$ . Since  $\mathbf{KK}^{+}$  is the orthogonal projection onto  $\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K})$ , we have  $\mathbf{KK}^{+}\hat{\mathbf{U}} = \hat{\mathbf{U}}$ , hence

$$
\begin{array}{l} \mathbf {K A B} ^ {\top} \mathbf {Q} ^ {\top} = \mathbf {K K} ^ {+} \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {K Q} ^ {\top} \\ = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\mathbf {U}} ^ {\top} \mathbf {U} \boldsymbol {\Sigma} \mathbf {V} ^ {\top} = \hat {\mathbf {U}} \hat {\boldsymbol {\Sigma}} \hat {\mathbf {V}} ^ {\top}. \\ \end{array}
$$

Therefore  $\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{K}^{+}\hat{\mathbf{U}}$  and  $\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{K}^{\top}\hat{\mathbf{U}}$  are optimal solutions to  $\min_{\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B}\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times R}}\| \mathbf{KAB}^{\top}\mathbf{Q}^{\top} - \mathbf{KQ}^{\top}\|_{F}$ .

The Moore-Penrose pseudo inverse of  $\mathbf{K}$  can be expressed through the SVD of  $\mathbf{K}$  as  $\mathbf{K}^{+} = \mathbf{V}_{K}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}^{-1}\mathbf{U}_{K}^{\top}$ . The singular value decomposition of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times T}$  can be computed efficiently as its rank is at most  $d$ . Indeed, we can first perform an SVD on  $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{U}_{K}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}\mathbf{V}_{K}^{\top}$  and  $\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{U}_{Q}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{Q}\mathbf{V}_{Q}^{\top}$ , then on the  $d \times d$  matrix  $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{K}\mathbf{V}_{K}^{\top}\mathbf{V}_{Q}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{Q} = \mathbf{U}'\boldsymbol{\Sigma}'\mathbf{V}'^{\top}$ . The SVD of  $\mathbf{KQ}^{\top}$  is then  $\mathbf{U}_{K}\mathbf{U}'\boldsymbol{\Sigma}'(\mathbf{V}_{Q}\mathbf{V}')^{\top} = \mathbf{U}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^{\top}$  with  $\mathbf{U} = \mathbf{U}_{K}\mathbf{U}' \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$  and  $\mathbf{V} = \mathbf{V}_{Q}\mathbf{V}' \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$ . This way the optimal solution provided by Theorem 2 can be computed efficiently in time  $\mathcal{O}(Td^{2})$ .

A similar approach is used by KQ-SVD to derive optimal projections for the low rank approximation of the product of the value cache with the output matrix (see Appendix B).
